title: Oliver versus Ory, then touring with Amos White and Nat Towles
summary: Red Allen's double band against Oliver, Oliver leaving, and Bill's road trip to Kansas City, Oklahoma and St. Louis with Creath.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: He still let it play with him that night and we had a double band. So me and John Joseph was on the bass and everything, so he said, Bill can you get another clarinet big band's coming back. I said sure, I can get red. They said come on Biffley, we call him Biffley. I said come on baby, we got a job tonight man. He said well, we're going to play against Kid Ora and them. Kid Ora and Oliver back at Me and Willa. Who was the trumpet?

Red Allen. Red Allen. We call him Biffley. I said he come on back there man, we blowed him out. We blowed him out, so these only had one trumpet, Ora had one trumpet, that was with Joe, that's all. I said Joe called us all kind of little young names as he always did, all kind of little young names and that's a human order had it. He had a few words about it. He wanted some more help. Ora said the jobs don't pay enough to have all that kind of help. I'm going to get mine. So he said yeah, let's get this little boy Lewis, get Lewis Armstrong to play with us. We going to kill New Orleans and kill him dead. Joe don't speak to me but Joe talk bad. He said we going to kill him dead. So finally they used, Joe, Joe used, Louis Armstrong on some engagements and there was the two best jazz trumpet players in the city of New Orleans. Louis Armstrong and Joe Oliver. Louis can tell you all about that. He know where he started from. So finally things went on good so Joe and Mac, Mary Mac had a few words down there and Joe said he was leaving. Joe left. Joe said when I come back to New Orleans, Jared Thomas would be the mayor. Jared Thomas would be president of the booze club. When I come back to New Orleans, Jared Thomas would be mayor. So when I finally again I saw Joe, he was down in Quincy, Florida. He had never come back no more. Never been made back. He had no further than Biloxian went back. He had Paul Barnes playing with him. Paul Barnes, Paul Barbaran. He had a bunch of New Orleans brothers come right to Biloxian and didn't come back to New Orleans. So when I finally heard that Joe was dead and we went on through. So one day I was playing my parade. Amos White, he come along, another great trumpet player. Amos White said, Billy, how about make the trip with me? I said, well, I was single and I didn't care where they go. He said, do North Louisiana man. Let's get away from you. Things just get tight. So we made up a band to go with old man Andrew Foster. He used to be a road band. That's where we went. My brother, baby, he was well. He said, well, Billy, I said, what? I said, you're going up there about Joe and him now. I know I ain't going to see you no more. Lewis and all of them up there. I said, I said, I don't say that man. It's like that. On a Sunday evening. So I went on, took my suitcase and I went. I was in Kansas City, Missouri on that Christmas Eve night. I got a telegram number. My brother was dead, buried today. So I didn't see him anymore. Which brother? Is that? That brother, baby. So I didn't see him anymore. So I kept going. I said, well, no need to come back. I kept going. I can't see him anymore. So I got around Kansas City, Missouri, played around there a little while. So this old boy plays so much banjo. He's young. With Nattoes. All of us, they're all young, all young. So I went through Oklahoma. He stayed in Oklahoma about 15 months. Bowling, Oklahoma. First time I ever saw a woman be mayor of a little time. So finally we went there and stayed there. It was doing so good. And we got a wire from Charlie Crest to come on to St. Louis, Billy. I've been knowing Charlie a long time. He's on the boat. He said, come on to St. Louis, Bill. So I went over to St. Louis. Then he put me in the jazz land, playing with him. So that's why our little band broke up. Amos White went to California. He's still in Oakland, California. Yes, I saw him. So he gave up with me.
Fess and I got two visits with him.
We were all left together. Frank Pass and all of us left. Nobody come back home but me. So while I come back home-
Who was leader of that band? Was that Nat Toe?
Nat Toe. He was the leader.
